extracted.intended_audience: journalists and news media professionals (reporters, editors, news organizations) including SPJ members
extracted.subtask_description: A code of ethics setting principles and concrete guidelines for gathering, reporting, and presenting news across media, including truth-seeking, minimizing harm, independence, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble — duty of the journalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conscientious journalists from all media and specialties strive to serve the public with thoroughness and honesty. Professional integrity is the cornerstone of a journalist's credibility. The code declares the Society's principles and standards of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section contains specific recommendations on verification, sourcing, representation, use of images, re-enactments, undercover reporting, plagiarism, cultural awareness, and separating news from advocacy or advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test the accuracy of information from all sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes verification and avoidance of both honest mistakes and intentional misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligently seek subjects to respond to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should make active efforts to contact people implicated in stories before publication so they can address or respond to allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer named sources and provide context on credibility; use anonymity only when necessary and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before promising anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat promises of anonymity as a serious commitment: verify motives, explain limits, and maintain confidentiality when promised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in headlines and promotional material
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that ancillary materials don't distort the story's meaning or emphasize misleading elements; maintain proportionality and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never distort the content of news photos or video
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label montages and photo illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When images are combined or altered for illustrative purposes, the audience must be informed; do not present altered imagery as straight documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged events
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged or reconstructed scenes should be rare and clearly identified so they are not mistaken for direct reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undercover or surreptitious methods except when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covert methods are a last resort and must be justified publicly within the reporting; explain why open methods failed and why the public interest outweighs deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present work honestly and credit sources properly; copying others' work without attribution is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the story of diversity and magnitude of human experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make editorial choices that reflect a wide range of experiences and perspectives rather than narrow or fashionable viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine own cultural values and avoid imposing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be reflective about bias and avoid judging subjects by the journalist's cultural norms; strive for cultural humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reporting and sourcing that resists reductive or prejudicial portrayals; seek diverse voices and avoid clichés.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support the open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect pluralism and include unpopular or dissenting perspectives so the public can judge them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include marginalized and less-visible sources where relevant; avoid privileging only official voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label opinion, analysis, and sponsored content so audiences do not conflate them with objective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid advertorials or sponsored content that masquerades as independent journalism; clearly disclose commercial relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure openness of public business
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate transparency in public institutions and use freedom-of-information tools to inform the public about governmental actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalists treat sources, subjects and colleagues as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section lists specific duties concerning compassion, sensitivity to trauma, privacy, taste, handling of juveniles and suspects, and balancing rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion for those harmed by coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be especially careful with vulnerable populations; avoid exploitative questioning or publicity that increases harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive when using interviews or photographs of grieving people
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing, consent, and the emotional state of subjects before pursuing or publishing such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting may cause harm or discomfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against potential harm and avoid gratuitous intrusion; do not use 'the public's right to know' as a blanket justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy of private people
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate treatment of public figures vs. private individuals; justify intrusion with clear, significant public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism and reporting choices that exploit tragedy or serve prurient interest rather than public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect minors and vulnerable victims by withholding identifying information unless there is compelling public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature identification that could damage reputations if charges are not filed; balance accuracy with fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider potential prejudice to legal proceedings when reporting on ongoing cases; avoid publishing material that could jeopardize due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be free of obligation to any interest other than the public's right to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section contains guidance on conflicts of interest, gifts, disclosures, advertiser influence, and resisting improper pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of financial, personal or political ties that could compromise or appear to compromise reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of associations that compromise integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate outside memberships and activities for potential impact on perceived neutrality and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts and shun secondary employment that compromise integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accepting benefits that could influence coverage; recuse from activities that create divided loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts cannot be avoided, be transparent with the audience about them so they can judge potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold those with power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative effort and critical scrutiny of public officials and institutions is a core duty despite pressures or risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from commercial partners; do not allow advertising relationships to shape news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pay for information in ways that create dependencies or distort motivations; verify paid-source information carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable (overarching principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are accountable to their readers, listeners, viewers and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section outlines practices for transparency, correction, dialogue with the public, and internal accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and explain news coverage; invite dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reporting choices, methods and limitations; provide avenues for public feedback and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage the public to voice grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote accessible complaint mechanisms and treat complaints seriously as part of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue clear corrections or clarifications when errors occur; do not hide or minimize mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical practices of journalists and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to call out colleagues and outlets when they fall short of ethical standards; internal policing is part of professional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by the same high standards held for others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply principles consistently to one's own reporting and behavior; avoid double standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical adoption and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics was adopted by the 1996 SPJ National Convention; earlier versions and revisions date to 1926, 1973, 1984, 1987 and 1996. The code is available in multiple languages and PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows institutional history, broad adoption, and availability of translations—useful when citing or applying the code internationally.
